hydration: Weigh yourself before and after. Replace 150% of what you lost — 1.5 L per kg dropped — with electrolyte, not plain water. This is not general wellness advice; for you it is the difference between a recovery session and a gout trigger.
myth: Ignore anything claiming sauna "sweats out uric acid". Measured urate in sweat is negligible to undetectable — your kidneys do that job, and sweating makes them worse at it, not better.
never: During an active flare — heat on an inflamed joint makes it worse, and the fluid loss compounds it.
When you are already behind on fluid, or the morning after alcohol.
Straight after a long run without drinking first. Rehydrate, then heat.
Alone in the house if you are pushing a long session.
